speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual; could you describe the appearance of the blisters on your forearm, and do you have a history of recurrent cold sores or genital herpes? I am also concerned about your immune system; have you been recently sick or taking any new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of skin blisters on the forearm and painful oral/genital ulcers is highly suggestive of a systemic autoimmune blistering disease rather than a simple viral infection, especially given your new medication. Did the blisters on your arm appear as small, grouped vesicles on an inflamed red base, or are they larger and tense? REQUEST TEST: Antibody panel including Anti-Desmoglein 1 and 2, Anti-BP180, and ANA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Antibody panel including Anti-Desmoglein 1 and 2, Anti-BP180, and ANA. Positive for Anti-Desmoglein antibodies (specifically Anti-Desmoglein 1 and 2); Anti-BP180 negative; ANA negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The positive Anti-Desmoglein 1 and 2 antibodies, combined with painful oral/genital ulcers and skin blisters, are diagnostic. I recommend you stop taking captopril immediately and begin high-dose systemic corticosteroids.
